changesets.title: Shop Golden Pear entry CTA dead-click root cause (Polar / Klaviyo interference hypothesis)
changesets.hypothesis: MS Clarity dashboard (2026-06-03 query via MCP) showed 603 dead clicks + 159 quickbacks on Shop Golden Pear entry CTA across /pages/golden-pear, last 4 days mobile. The CTA appears on homepage banner, partner LPs (roman-atwood, cleetus), and the GP LP itself (hero / footer / winners re-CTA). All CTAs ALREADY have proper href values (#ks-gp-shop or shopify://pages/golden-pear) — verified via theme repo grep. The dead-click pattern is NOT a missing-href issue. Two leading hypotheses: (1) Polar Analytics cart-injector intercepting anchor clicks — visible in the live console as [Polar] Cart interception setup complete. If the Polar handler is over-broad it could swallow same-origin anchor clicks even on non-cart links. (2) Klaviyo onsite popup backdrop persisting as transparent overlay after close, catching the next tap (CSS z-index / pointer-events bug). Reproducible scenario in a Clarity replay (06-01 16:48:06 session): user closes a Close dialog popup, THEN dead-clicks Shop Golden Pear — rules out the popup itself blocking, points to residual overlay or interceptor.
changesets.notes: Spawned from CS-2026-191 diagnostic phase. CS-191 shipped the thumbnail-swap + ATC delegation fixes (PR #79, merge cce6707). This CS handles the remaining ~603/4d dead-click leak that CS-191 did NOT fix. Diagnostic path: (a) On a preview theme, toggle Polar Analytics app embed OFF, reproduce dead-click attempt on Shop Golden Pear CTAs — if fixed, Polar is the culprit; file vendor ticket. (b) If Polar is innocent, instrument the page with a document-level click listener logging event.defaultPrevented + event.target + event.currentTarget, reproduce on mobile to identify the swallower. (c) Inspect DOM after closing a Klaviyo popup for orphaned modal-backdrop divs with non-auto pointer-events.

expected_impact.balancing_impact: dead_clicks_per_1k_sessions on Shop Golden Pear CTA elements
expected_impact.L1_outcome: Recover residual dead-click leak post-CS-191 (~$200-300/wk estimated)
expected_impact.L4_learning: Third-party app interception of same-origin anchor clicks — first known instance for Polar; informs vendor selection criteria for cart-replacement apps.
